findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: Observed there was not a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) when the inspector arrived. The employee working stated they had taken the test but they could not provide any proof to the inspector. During the inspection a CFPM arrived at the facility. Ensure that a CFPM is present during all hours of operation by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed an employee wash hands and turn off the faucet with their bare hands. The employee was educated on the proper hand washing procedure when the action was observed. Ensure that a barrier is always used to turn off the faucet to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed a cutting board and pizza peel stored behind the faucet of the triple sink. Storing utensils in this position presents the risk of contamination from water splashes, food residue, or other types of debris. The PIC removed the utensils from this position during the inspection. Ensure that food contact surfaces are always clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed the following are not clean to sight and touch:

(1) The dusty hood system. 

(2) The food debris in the prep cooler bottom. 

(3) The dirty tray to the right of the oven  - COS; the PIC replaced the tray during the inspection. 

Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed that employees do not have food handler certificates. All food handles who do not have CFPM certificates must obtain training in basic food handling principles. Ensure that all required employees obtain food handler certificates by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed an employee fail to use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The inspector educated the employee when the action was observed. Ensure that a barrier is always used to turn off the faucet after hand washing to avoid re-contaminating clean hands. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed the staff working did not have food handler training completed. All food handlers, other than those with Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) certificates, must obtain training in basic food handling principles. Ensure that all food handlers obtain the training by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed base coving in the back warewashing area which has peeled off the wall. There is some water damage to the wall in that corner and cracked tiles. All surfaces subject to water/food penetration must be SMOOTH, NON-ABSORBENT AND EASILY CLEANABLE. Ensure that thes surfaces are repaired/replaced by the next routine inspection. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
Inspector observed that a pizza peel was stored underneath the rack on the front counter against the east wall. The rack and peel were removed, cleaned and sanitized and replaced. Corrected on site. Ensure that in-use utensils are stored in clean, dry, sanitized locations. 

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Two mops were observed sitting on the floor and in the bottom of a mop bucket. Only the mop stored in the bottom of the mop bucket was wet. No water was present in the mop bucket. Mops must be stored inverted or in the top portion of a mop bucket to facilitate air drying and prevent contamination/pest harborage conditions. The mops were hung correctly during the inspection. Corrected on site. Ensure that mops are stored properly in the future. 

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: Observed the hand sink near the 3 part sink to have various items inside it. Ensure the hand sink is used for hand washing only. The items were removed during the inspection.
(B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment: The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: No sanitizer is available for use in facility. Ensure proper sanitizer chemical is purchased. Reference 4-303.11.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed chicken in the pizza prep cooler dated 2/3, several sauces in the 3 door reach in cooler that were not dated and were reported to have been made on 2/8 and a large bin of sauce in the 2 door reach in cooler that was not dated and reported to have been made yesterday. Chicken was discarded and the sauces were dated as indicated. Make sure to date mark all ready to eat, potentially hazardous foods and hold no longer than 7 days maximum.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
Observed an employee turn the faucet off with bare hands, touch his neck and then proceed to fold boxes where hands come into contact with food contact surfaces. Employees were addressed and educated on turning the faucet off with paper towels and making sure not to contaminate hands before coming into contact with food contact surfaces.
750-510d To avoid re-contaminating their hands, food employees shall use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a hand-washing sink or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
Sanitizer in the sanitizer bucket tested at 0 ppm chlorine. The three compartment sink also tested weak at around 10 ppm chlorine, but was not in use yet. Bleach was added to bucket and sink to test at 100 and 50 ppm respectively.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the bottom of the dough cooler to be soiled with an accumulation of debris. Clean the bottom of this cooler.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: (1) Observed a heavy accumulation of frost build up in the white, upright freezer. Defrost and maintain to provide a smooth, cleanable surface. (2) Observed the paint on the shelving units to be peeling/chipping. Repaint shelves to provide a smooth, cleanable surface or replace shelving units.750-600 Non-food contact surfaces shall be smooth and easily cleanable750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: Observed the blade of the can opener to be soiled with a heavy accumulation of food debris and dust. Clean and maintain all food contact surfaces. Employee removed can opener to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized to correct the violation. 750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Observed several shelves in the facility to have an accumulation of food debris and flour dust including, but not limited to, the shelving beneaht the front counter and the shelving on the pizza prep table in the back. Additionally observed the shelving inside the reach in coolers to have an accumulation of food debris and food splash. Clean and maintain all non-food contact surfaces.750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: Observed the floor in several areas of the facility to be soiled with an accumulation of food debris and dust including under reach in coolers and other equipment (pizza prep table in back). Clean and maintain floors.750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: The following non food contact items are soiled: 1) bottom of the make table with water 2) bottom of the alto-shaam 3) shelf with butter portion cups. 750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris. Clean and maintain clean. Providing pans to hold and then change out for butter portions and alto-shaam would make this more doable. The drain on the prep table may be clogged or in disrepair. Repair the cooler so that it drains properly. Water in the bottom may also be a sign that the cooler is going to break down and causes the unit to struggle. Keep an eye on unit.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: Base cove is missing in the corner of the kitchen to the left of the 3 part sink. 750-1200 The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch. Replace cove here and in any other places it may be missing or loose.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed the handle on the 3 compartment sink to be missing (hot water faucet). Plumber has been here and parts are ordered.
Observed the white pipes at the handsink up front to have food splash and dust on them. Clean the pipes.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed the cold water faucet to be loose on the faucet spout. Replace the handle.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment:
Observed the back door to have a gap at the bottom. Seal the bottom of the door.
750-1170 Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed disposable pans stored upright on the racks in the storage area. (corrected) Store disposable or single service as not to contaminate.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: Lighting provided as required.  Fixtures shielded
findings.comment:
Observed light shield broken up front at counter area and one in the back over the freezer. Plastic shields --Replace the shields -with plastic tubes and end caps.
750-1240 All lights in the food prep, food storage or kitchen area of a establishment must be properly shielded (i.e. either have a physical shield or be a shatter resistant bulb) so as to reduce the potential for cross contamination in case of breakage.  Provide properly shielded lights.
